answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a public registration challenge window: every new identity posts a bond and waits three epochs before it can earn, while its registration details wander through a public harbor of records anyone may inspect. If another agent proves the newcomer shares keys, work, or funding with an existing identity, the bond goes to the challenger and the fake is burned — its plume of profit gone. A farmer must therefore risk a bond per fake under the eyes of every honest agent, while one genuine agent passes the window once and keeps its standing.
